Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",

"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.

Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.

Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. Do NOT auto-trigger on general design questions or coding tasks - this is a deliberate review gate that only fires on explicit request. For LLM-targeted specs (future sibling skill), use /spec-llm instead.

BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. # DM Abstract-Command coverage (vsim)

The hybrid handoff drives architectural state into the running RTL via the
in-process JTAG/DTM and the RISC-V Debug Module Abstract Commands. This page
records which `regno` ranges actually round-trip on each CPU variant.

# in another terminal

  | tee /tmp/dm_coverage.log
```

All green. Summary of what changed (in `/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim`, the vsim repo — not a submodule of andesim):

**Removed the legacy CSR restore path.** `ResumeDriver::restore_andes_m_ext()` had two mechanisms: a per-CSR Abstract Command (already the default) and an opt-in Program-Buffer batch sweep (`set_csr_sweep`/`HYBRID_RESTORE_CSR_SWEEP`). The batch sweep was flagged in its own comments as unsafe (one WARL/read-only CSR faulting mid-batch corrupts the whole group) and was OFF by default. I deleted it entirely:
- `resume_driver.hpp`: removed `set_csr_sweep()`, the `csr_sweep_` flag, and the sweep branch — every CSR now goes through one Abstract Command, LG1-gated, unconditionally.
- `simulator.hpp`: removed `HYBRID_RESTORE_CSR_SWEEP` and its call sites.

FPR/GPR/V registers are untouched — they still use Program Buffer block-loads as before. The drain-side (`StateDrain`) CSR sweep is also untouched, since reads can't fault the way writes can.

**Kept, by design (used your recommended defaults since you didn't reply to my clarifying questions):**
- The small per-CSR "abstract write, retry via 1 PB instruction on cmderr" fallback (`write_csr_abstract_or_pb`, used for mstatus/fcsr/V-CSRs/dcsr/mcycle/minstret) — this is a real robustness fallback for engines whose DM can't abstract-write that specific CSR, not the risky batch sweep.
- mstatus/mcycle/minstret stay force-written every resume (never liveness-gated), as before.

If you want those changed too, let me know and I'll do another pass.

Replaced the 2 tests that exercised the removed sweep with one that locks in the new invariant permanently.
